title: A five minute recording exports in less time than it plays
goal: Writing a five minute screen recording out as a 1080p video takes nearly six minutes, longer than the recording itself runs. Premiere and share tools write a screen recording several times faster than it plays; people should not wait longer for the file than the video lasts.
notes: Measured 2026-09-24 during the-export-sheet-lets-you-pick-the-size-of-the-v: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/export-a-video-at-1080p-walk.json --no-build -> [20 writeVideo] five-minutes-at-1080p.mp4 is 17 MB, written in 342447 ms; it runs 319.24s at 1728 x 1080 px ... made frame by frame from the document. Load average about 3-4 at the time. Path: EditorState.writeVideo -> DocumentFrames (composites every frame at canvas size 2880x1800, then DocumentMovieWriter fits to plan.size). Likely wins: composite at the output size rather than the canvas size, decode with hardware, pipeline frame fetch and encode. An untouched recording at Full is still a verbatim copy and is not affected.
acceptance: The five minute Retina talk, with captions burned in, writes at 1080p in under half its running time on this Mac
The export card still moves smoothly and the editor stays responsive while it writes
export-a-video-at-1080p-walk logs the time the write took and still lands a 1728 x 1080 file

log.note: baseline 2026-09-27 21:36: export-a-video-at-1080p-walk wrote five minutes (319.24s) at 1728x1080 in 337799 ms, load ~4. Path: one AVAssetImageGenerator seek per frame at 2880x1800, composite at canvas size, CPU scale into the pixel buffer, all serial.

adversarial pass: a Premiere user expects export faster than realtime; the write was serial per-frame seeks at 2880x1800, then a CPU shrink. Fix: front-to-back reader, composite at output size. Colour check: stream and generator frames match pixel for pixel ([48,55,68] both, Rec.709 space). 12 export walks + captions-from-the-sound + an-editing-session all ok. Full suite green (10223 tests).

left rough: a ~300ms main-thread stall right when an export starts. It is there on the old path too (measured by swapping back), and the setup work on the main actor is <0.1ms, so the stall is elsewhere (SwiftUI layout when the card appears?). Not filed: one stall at the click that starts the export, hard to see behind the save panel closing. Also left rough: rotated-track recordings still take the slow generator path.

Five minute Retina talk with captions writes at 1080p in 72-83s (0.23-0.26 of its 319s), down from 338s. Front-to-back clip reader (MovieFrameStream) and compositing at output size. export-a-video-at-1080p-walk logs the pace and holds it to 0.5, and still lands 1728x1080. New export-card-while-writing-walk photographs the card mid-write; the main thread's busiest slice while writing is 15-18ms. Full suite green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-27-fast-video-export.json.
